newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent indicators flag buy signals.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent indicators flag buy signals.

text.p: ARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* Brent to see some short term stability supported by short-covering ahead of the July Brent expiry and with a clutch of indicators flagging buy signals.
* Open interest positions on NYMEX crude July options, which expire at the end of business today, indicate there could be a move towards $19 per barrel or even $19.50.

IPE Brent crude futures may continue to see some short term stability supported by short-covering ahead of the July Brent expiry and with a clutch of indicators flagging buy signals, but some analysts remain bearish in the longer term.

Charles Gray at Prudential Bache said: "The market may have some room to creep higher with stochastics very close to crossing, offering a buy signal, in fact if you look at the NYMEX chart the stochastics for all the contracts have already crossed".
He said that the overall feeling of a loss of momentum to the downside was also giving some support to the current levels.
"Long term momentum indicators are also coming to the point where they are getting closer too," Gray said.
Traders and analysts said open interest positions on NYMEX crude July options, which expire at the end of business today, indicate there could be a move towards $19 per barrel or even $19.50.
Independent analyst Elli Gifford was more bearish.
"Brent is unwinding its oversold position but I don't see much chance of it going higher, in fact it may be about to go down again".
She saw resistance in the $17.60-$17.90 range with a possible "slide off" to $17.20 per barrel.
On gas oil she said gap down resistance around $164.25 on the July chart with support coming in at $161.25 a tonne.
"I think this market will hold for now, but I suspect in the somewhat longer term there may be more falls," Gifford said.
Gray said an Island reversal pattern on the spot month continuation chart for gas oil could point the market higher, but he said he was wary of an Island reversal pattern on the back of a rollover.
"This gives a bit of a false picture, but generally the market is looking for a basing point," he added.
SIMEX July Brent futures were firmer on Friday with some short-covering expected ahead of the weekend providing some support for the contract ahead of expiry at close of business in London today.
July was last traded at $17.60 per barrel on SIMEX. August was last traded at $17.90 per barrel.
Brokers said a firmer tone on NYMEX was also supporting the market. NYMEX July futures were last traded on ACCESS at $18.95 per barrel, up 26 cents from Thursday's the close.
Gasoline futures were up around 0.42 at 57.50 cents a gallon on ACCESS, while heating oil was up 0.58 from Thursday's close at 52.20 cents a gallon.
Fundamentally the market has been getting some lift from reports of a potential hold up in resuming oil sales under the Iraqi-United Nations "oil-for-food" deal, traders said.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
